findings.summary: assertGitHubRepo/assertAzureDevOpsRepo/assertGitLabRepo throw plain Error while equivalent validation elsewhere throws ValidationError
evidence: repo-detector.ts:64: throw new Error(`${context} requires GitHub repositories. Got: ${repoInfo.type}`);
repo-detector.ts:79: throw new Error(`${context} requires Azure DevOps repositories. Got: ${repoInfo.type}`);
repo-detector.ts:94: throw new Error(`${context} requires GitLab repositories. Got: ${repoInfo.type}`);
graphql-commit-strategy.ts:124: throw new ValidationError(`GraphQL commit strategy requires GitHub repositories. Got: ${repoInfo.type}`);
repo-detector.ts:198: throw new ValidationError(`Unrecognized git URL format: ${gitUrl}...`)
findings.suggestion: Change assertGitHubRepo, assertAzureDevOpsRepo, and assertGitLabRepo to throw ValidationError instead of plain Error, consistent with detectRepoType and the GraphQL commit strategy's equivalent check. These are all input validation — wrong repo type passed to a platform-specific function.

findings.summary: GraphQL error responses throw plain Error with inconsistent message formats
evidence: graphql-commit-strategy.ts:296: throw new Error(`GraphQL error: ${parsed.errors.map((e) => e.message).join(', ')}`);
graphql-commit-strategy.ts:303: throw new Error('GraphQL response missing commit OID');
graphql-commit-strategy.ts:468: throw new Error(`GraphQL error: ${parsed.errors.map((e) => e.message).join(', ')}`);
graphql-commit-strategy.ts:498: throw new Error(`GraphQL response missing repository ID for ${repoInfo.owner}/${repoInfo.repo}`);
graphql-commit-strategy.ts:412: return new Error(`GraphQL commit failed for ${repo}: ${cleanMessage}`);
findings.suggestion: The GraphQL strategy has three different error message formats for API failures: 'GraphQL error: ...', 'GraphQL response missing ...', and 'GraphQL commit failed for ...'. Consider standardizing the prefix or using a dedicated error class for GraphQL API errors to make them easier to identify in catch blocks and retry logic.
